alternatives.concept: Mathematics, statistical inference and econometrics are combined with economics, programming, algorithms and computational optimisation to study quantitative economic and business problems.
alternatives.weightLimit: This unique-course group documents actual emphasis rather than an approval threshold. Additional computational/economic content is separately traced; no course counted twice in a programme.
alternatives.limits: No second/advanced econometrics sequence, dedicated time series, required forecasting seminar or guaranteed thesis replacement.
alternatives.progressionReview: Programming and introductory economics begin in Semester 1, followed by calculus and research/statistics foundations. Linear algebra, probability, machine learning and Algorithms & Data Structures precede advanced algorithms and optimisation. Multivariate statistics precedes Econometrics. Advanced Calculus is offered only in the final spring after its gateway prerequisite is feasible; it therefore follows optimisation, rather than being claimed as an earlier foundation. Introductory economics supports Public Economics before the later specialised microeconomics course. All formal prerequisites and term offerings are checked separately.

alternatives.concept: Mathematics, statistics and econometrics are combined with programming, software, databases, machine learning and neural networks, emphasising how data are organised and used to build predictive models.
alternatives.weightLimit: This unique-course group documents actual emphasis rather than an approval threshold. Additional computational/economic content is separately traced; no course counted twice in a programme.
alternatives.additionalScope: Computational/data-science methods, not extra specialist econometrics
alternatives.limits: No second/advanced econometrics sequence, dedicated time series, required forecasting seminar or guaranteed thesis replacement.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest-match curriculum, this route replaces accounting/corporate finance, public economics, numerical methods and general ethics with database management, software development, neural networks, AI ethics and explicit AI/business applications. Those changes make computational data science and predictive modelling, rather than the broad economics-and-operations-research core, the additional organising logic.
alternatives.progressionReview: Programming, data handling and economics start in Semester 1. Mathematical Methods and Research Methods & Statistics precede linear algebra, probability and machine learning. Algorithms & Data Structures precedes Advanced Algorithms, and machine learning precedes neural networks. Multivariate statistics is placed before Econometrics. Logic is later than advanced algorithms, but the introductory programming course already supplies elementary logic/sets and the formal prerequisite; no extra prerequisite is invented.

academicReview.logisticsCandidate: Rejected: algorithmic optimisation is substantive but not enough to establish the defining logistics/supply-chain domain. No adjacent organisational courses are used to fill a24-course logistics programme.
academicReview.financeChallenge: The original third programme is mathematically coherent, but the finance-specific work is practical decision-making/accounting. Money, Banking & Finance formally requires Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, whose actual content is venture creation, customer validation and a startup pitch. Prerequisite status and generic business context do not establish its substantive contribution to the evidenced quantitative-finance direction. Broadening the concept after seeing that course would conceal the defect. Removing the finance course/prerequisite leaves no separately evidenced finance curriculum beyond the closest option’s accounting/economic core; arbitrary substitutions cannot establish distinctness. This is not a financial-course quota or a demand for full disciplinary equivalence.
academicReview.stoppingDecision: Two programmes survive the source-first course/concept challenge: quantitative economics with optimisation, and computational data science with econometrics. Logistics remains rejected because optimisation/algorithms alone do not supply the defining logistics/supply-chain domain. The finance candidate was retested against actual course content: practical finance requires a venture-creation course whose role had been defended only by prerequisite status and generic business context. These do not establish its contribution to a quantitative-finance concept. Removing that pair leaves no distinct finance-specific curriculum beyond the closest programme’s accounting/economic study; replacing it with financial law or unrelated business courses would add adjacency rather than the missing quantitative enquiry. The third option is removed, not relabelled or padded. Every generator row retains one core/candidate owner; no third option is manufactured.
academicReview.sourceFirstStatus: Passed separately identified same-AI final pass3 on exact05325b2 canonical/decision blobs after the earlier rejection of the third option and bounded mathematical-depth correction. Both remaining programmes substantively respond to the defining external quantitative inquiry; caveats and coherence were not treated as sufficient.

finalDecisions.rationale: UCR introduces differentiation, integration and differential equations. These supply a calculus foundation related to the external introductory analysis strand. This is a partial mathematical relationship, not a verified identical course-specific topic list or proof level.
